blocks.text: In use · Ceremonial Ribbon · Quarter awards
High Honors recognizes effort selected by a teacher. The Divine Code ribbon carries zero to four clasps for an awarded quarter; each clasp acknowledges additional effort.

Placement: Classroom honour implemented in the game and teacher character manager. Assigned by a teacher for a year and quarter. The ribbon displays the latest awarded quarter; earlier awards remain recorded.
Reward: Every skill cap +5 for the ribbon, plus +2 per clasp: +5, +7, +9, +11, or +13. Only the strongest quarter applies; quarters do not stack. Train to earn the extra levels.

Fictional lore — The Divine Code: In the tradition of this ribbon, the Divine Code is a luminous pattern revealed through patient work. It becomes clearer whenever someone practices, revises, asks for help, or returns to a difficult task. Its galaxy-colored folds hold many small points of light, each recalling an attempt that mattered. The long center ribbon carries up to four clasps: visible marks of effort that has been seen and valued. The blue flower at its heart represents the understanding that grows from continuing to try. Design history: originally called Galaxy Gala; combines the Rosewater Gala layers with the Celestial Fanfare crest, pale-blue backing ribbons and blue flower brooch. The central purple tail extends slightly below the others. The teacher selects recipients. Each quarter is recorded separately; only the strongest quarter contributes the skill-cap bonus.
